clue.text: Wife breaks ice, potentially, in stuffy atmosphere

indicators.note: the wife's letter breaks into the frozen word, splitting it open

parts.note: frost is ice in the making, so potentially ice

explanation.surface: A wife shatters the frosty mood in a stuffy room.
explanation.definitionFit: A frowst is a warm, stale, fuggy air in a closed room, a stuffy atmosphere.

clue.text: Mounted policeman perhaps corners a looter

indicators.note: the horseman's word corners the letter, surrounding it

parts.note: a mounted policeman is an example of a rider on horseback

explanation.surface: A mounted officer traps a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider plunders, so is a looter.

clue.text: Sew up attempt to host foreign dignitary in part of UK

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the attempt holds the dignitary inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a count is a continental nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stitch up a deal hosting a visiting nobleman in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEW into WES, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Country is the south-western region of England, part of the UK.

clue.text: Developed trendy idea right away, making colourful clothing

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters being worked into a new form
away tells us to take the right letter out

explanation.surface: A designer develops a fashionable idea for bright clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from TRENDY IDEA, leaving TENDYIDEA for 'Developed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dye is a technique producing brightly patterned garments, colourful clothing.

clue.text: Learner, one into various octaves — not English singer

indicators.note: the learner and the one go into the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of octaves in a varied order
not tells us to leave the English letter out of octaves

parts.note: L is a learner, as on an L-plate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A singing pupil works through several octaves, but not in an English style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' drops E from OCTAVES; 'various' shuffles OCTAVS to VOCAST, and 'into' puts L and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is a singer, especially in a band.

clue.text: Salad dressing, given a shake, at last runnier

indicators.note: a shake mixes up the letters of the two words beside it
at last asks for the final letter

explanation.surface: A dressing shaken until it becomes thinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a shake' looks like one instruction about the dressing; 'given a' is the fodder and 'shake' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid used to dress salads.

clue.text: Quickly made stroke in pool competition

definitions.text: Quickly made stroke in pool competition

parts.words: Quickly made stroke in pool competition
parts.note: the fastest swimming stroke, used in freestyle races in a pool

explanation.definitionFit: The front crawl is the fastest swimming stroke, used in freestyle races.

clue.text: Revolutionary artist I rejected as a boy

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so read backwards
rejected tells us to remove the letter I

parts.note: Salvador Dali, the surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A rebel painter turned down as a youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I rejected' drops I from DALI to leave DAL, which 'Revolutionary' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man.

clue.text: Having the cheek to criticise a pot-boiler?

parts.note: sauce is impudence, cheek
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Having the nerve to slate a cheap formulaic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A pot-boiler is usually a hack novel; here it is literally something that boils a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is literally a pot for boiling, a witty reading of pot-boiler.

clue.text: One from Germany that's twice written about primarily space and time

definitions.text: One from Germany that's twice written about primarily space and time

indicators.note: the two copies are written around the initials, enclosing them
twice means the German word is used two times

parts.note: ein is German for one

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A German-born figure whose work concerned space and time.
explanation.walkthrough: The German 'ein' doubled, with S and T between the two copies; the whole clue also describes the physicist famed for relativity of space and time.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist of relativity was born in Germany and wrote about space and time.

clue.text: Difficult time, dropping aitches, causing some heat

indicators.note: a Cockney-style speaker drops the letter h from each word

parts.note: hard means difficult
an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A tough period, spoken in a dropped-h accent, stirs up passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate warmth of feeling, so a figurative heat.

clue.text: Guiding light having to do time inside?

definitions.meaning: a signal fire or lamp that guides ships or travellers
read as three words, to ... (convict) is to serve time in prison

explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light that guides, and split up it reads as being a convict.

clue.text: Swift traveller booked some time ago

definitions.text: Swift traveller booked some time ago

parts.words: Swift traveller booked some time ago
parts.note: a traveller created by Jonathan Swift, who appeared in a book centuries ago; Swift reads as fast

explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Swift's 1726 satirical novel of voyages is a famous fictional traveller.

clue.text: Advantageous position — last song on the LP?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a favoured position, from the inner lane on a racetrack
on a vinyl record the final song lies nearest the centre

explanation.definitionFit: The inner lane gives runners an advantage, and the last song on a record lies innermost.

clue.text: Locks may be here, as information is kept secret

definitions.meaning: hair (locks) sits beneath a person's headgear
an idiom for keeping information confidential

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keeping something private; literally hair lies beneath a hat.

clue.text: One's just prepared for the new term

definitions.text: One's just prepared for the new term

parts.words: One's just prepared for the new term
parts.note: reads like a pupil ready for school, but describes a freshly coined word

explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression.

clue.text: A fellow well able to speak the language of the rich

parts.words: well able to speak the language
parts.note: fluent means speaking a language easily

explanation.surface: A man who speaks the tongue of the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, rich.

clue.text: Where unreleased tracks are not to be broadcast

definitions.meaning: songs left off a disc are literally not on the album
an idiom for remarks not meant for publication

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unofficial and not for publication, and literally describes songs left off an album.

clue.text: Set aside attention given to biblical writer

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
Mark wrote the second Gospel

explanation.surface: Putting aside time to listen to a gospel author.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside for a purpose.

clue.text: A desk in the office

explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a writing desk and also an office or agency.

clue.text: Don't be unreasonable — the production's not too bad

definitions.meaning: a theatrical show that is passable or middling

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an urge to behave justly, and can also describe a show that is middling.

clue.text: Potential violence? In the past, old king intervened

indicators.note: the king comes between letters of the past word, inside it

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Trouble brewed in the old days when a monarch stepped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble, threatened violence.

clue.text: Choose not to work with ticket salesman

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tout sells tickets unofficially, often at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Someone declines to deal with a ticket tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline to take part is to choose not to participate.

clue.text: Mate, perhaps, has aged so terribly

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters being badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend has grown old dreadfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a pal, but it is a ship's officer, an example of an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's mate is an example of an experienced sailor, a crossword-familiar term for an old salt.

clue.text: Go down for a swim

explanation.definitionFit: To dip is to go down, and a dip is a brief swim.

clue.text: Ad I meant to be distributed in cartoon form

indicators.note: distributed suggests spreading the letters out into a new order

explanation.surface: An advert designed to be released as a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated films are made in cartoon form.

clue.text: Silence crowing — it may interrupt the flow

parts.note: to stop something is to silence it
a cock is the bird that crows

explanation.surface: Shutting up a boastful person interrupts their flow of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve that shuts off the flow of water in a pipe.

clue.text: Invent type of paint

definitions.meaning: to fabricate or concoct a story

explanation.definitionFit: To make up a story is to invent it, and make-up is cosmetic face paint.
